name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
Information Systems - academic year 23/24
Course Project
Scenario

La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of materials and products for the home. To improve the efficiency of its operations and the service to customers, the company is re-designing its information system. The details follow.

La Reine Marlene has a wide network of suppliers. The suppliers of La Reine Marlene will have to register in the system, providing their credentials and company details, including VAT number, address and the IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can make proposals of their own products by entering in the system the following information for each product: category, sale price (the one that La Reine Marlene must pay to the supplier), availability, photo, description, guaranteed delivery time. The product categories are 16: Garden, Bathroom, Air Conditioning, Lighting, Decoration, Flooring, Doors and Windows, Carpentry, Kitchen, Storage, Tools, Electricity, Construction, Paints, Hardware, Furniture. Once a proposal has been entered, the supplier can no longer modify it until they receive a response notification.

When a supplier enters a proposal, the administration department of La Reine Marlene receives a message notifying the presence of a new proposal from the suppliers. At that point, it must verify the proposal and select one of the following options: Order accepted, Revisions requested, Order rejected. If the order is accepted, a separate order management process will start, to which the information on the price to be displayed in the store is added, so that this information will already be available in the subsequent processes. If instead revisions have been requested, they must be made explicit in a comment: at that point the supplier receives a notification and has 5 working days to modify the proposal, entering reply comments, and re-submit it. If the proposal has been modified within the 5 working days, then the proposal evaluation process restarts, otherwise the proposal is deleted from the system and the supplier notified. The administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours about the presence of a proposal that is waiting to be validated. A proposal that has not been verified within 10 working days is automatically rejected, and a specific message is sent to the supplier.

Once the products ordered from the suppliers are shipped and arrive at the destination La Reine Marlene site (there are dozens of them throughout Italy), they are entered in the inventory of all the products available in the store (La Reine Marlene has no warehouse: any available product is on display). Each product is catalogued according to its category, available quantity and location in the store. The location in the store is entered directly by the goods receiving staff: when an order is delivered, the staff members must verify each product. If there are no problems, the operator confirms the product and the system proposes a list of possible placements: the location is chosen, and the product is physically handed over to whoever will take care of its placement in the store and of printing the price to be displayed. Should there be problems with any product, the operator reports it by entering a comment and the product does not enter the store. At the end of these operations of verification of an order arrival, the operator closes the procedure and a new process starts, managed by the order department: if all the products have been accepted, the order is concluded and the payment sent. Otherwise, the order is updated and a new arrival that completes it is awaited. In both cases specific messages are sent to the supplier.

The system keeps track of stock in real time. An automatic notification is sent to the order department when a product reaches a critical reorder level (where it is specified). The administrators, in fact, can schedule automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products, in order to maintain an optimal inventory. In case of automatic reordering, a message is sent to the pre-established supplier, who has two working days to confirm acceptance of the order. In the absence of critical thresholds and of the related automation, the new order is managed by the order department with a separate process.

Customers looking for materials for the home can purchase the products both through the physical store and through the online store. In the online store, customers who have registered on the site can browse the digital catalogue, specify the desired products and quantities and complete the order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs. Customers can choose among different payment options: credit card (Visa or Mastercard), Paypal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchasing card, or immediate online bank transfer with the affiliated banks. Once the order is paid, the system keeps track of deliveries in real time. Customers receive a link by email through which they can follow the status of their shipments. In addition, those who have given consent to the use of the mobile phone number will receive notifications on updates to delivery times. Once the product arrives at its destination, the order is tracked as concluded. Deliveries are managed by partner companies, and each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping carrier. Consider that the online store is also accessible through a dedicated app: the operations and procedures are the same as those of the site.

La Reine Marlene offers a complete customer service through the information system. Customers can ask questions, request assistance or make complaints directly through the system. Support tickets are automatically assigned to a customer service agent. Every time a ticket is assigned, the agent receives a notification and has 24 hours to respond (if this does not happen, the ticket is reassigned to a new operator, and the statistics updated). The customer is informed upon receipt of the reply message, and has five working days to respond: otherwise, the ticket is considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, customer support. These data are used to analyze performance and make strategic decisions.
highLevelGoals: Suppliers need to efficiently register their company details and submit product proposals, ensuring all necessary information is captured and managed throughout the proposal lifecycle.
Suppliers must receive clear and prompt notifications about the acceptance, rejection, or requested revisions of their product proposals, and be able to respond to revision requests effectively.
Suppliers should be able to quickly confirm acceptance of automatic reorders from La Reine Marlene to ensure continuous supply.

The administration department staff must be able to promptly review, evaluate, and respond to new supplier product proposals, including requesting revisions or rejecting proposals, to maintain an efficient procurement process.

The system should ensure that administration department staff are reminded of and proposals are automatically processed if not verified within specified timeframes, preventing bottlenecks in the proposal evaluation process.

Goods receiving staff must be able to verify incoming products, confirm their receipt, and accurately assign their placement within the store, or report issues to prevent faulty products from entering inventory.
Order department staff must be notified of critical stock levels and be able to manage new orders efficiently, whether through automated reordering or manual processes, to maintain optimal inventory.

Order department staff must be able to finalize orders and initiate payments to suppliers when all products are accepted, or update orders and await further arrivals if products are not fully accepted.
Customers must be able to easily browse the digital catalogue, select products, complete online orders, make secure payments, and track their deliveries in real-time.
The system must facilitate the process of customers purchasing products directly from the physical store, including managing inventory and sales data related to in-store transactions.
Customers must be able to easily submit support tickets for inquiries or complaints and receive timely responses, with the ability to follow up on their tickets.
Customer service agents must receive timely notifications for assigned tickets and be able to respond within specified timeframes to ensure high-quality customer service.
Shipping carriers must be able to manage and track the delivery status of assigned online purchases, providing real-time updates to customers.
Managers/Executives need to access and analyze comprehensive data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support to assess performance and inform strategic business decisions.
Administrators must be able to configure and schedule automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products to maintain optimal inventory levels and prevent stockouts.
lowLevelGoals: Suppliers can submit their company name, contact information, and business registration documents through a dedicated API endpoint.
Suppliers can create a new product proposal by providing product name, description, pricing, category (from 16 specific categories), availability, photo, and guaranteed delivery time via an API call.
Suppliers can retrieve a list of their submitted proposals and their current status (e.g., 'pending', 'accepted', 'rejected', 'revisions requested') through an API query.
The system sends automated email or in-app notifications to suppliers when their proposal status changes (e.g., 'accepted', 'rejected', 'revisions requested').

Suppliers can update an existing proposal with new information and resubmit it for review via an API endpoint, referencing the original proposal ID, and including reply comments within 5 working days.
Suppliers can accept an automated reorder request by sending a confirmation signal to the system via a dedicated API endpoint.
If a supplier does not confirm an automatic reorder within 2 working days, the system automatically rejects the reorder and notifies the Order Department staff.
Staff can query the system to get a list of all product proposals awaiting review, including supplier details and submission date.
Staff can change the status of a specific proposal to 'accepted' via an API call, triggering notifications to the supplier and initiating the order management process.
Staff can change the status of a specific proposal to 'rejected' and provide a reason via an API call, triggering notifications to the supplier.
Staff can change the status of a specific proposal to 'revisions requested' and specify required changes via an API call, triggering notifications to the supplier.
Staff can create a new purchase order for an accepted product proposal, specifying initial quantities and linking it to the supplier, via an API endpoint.
Staff can define the selling price for a product associated with an accepted proposal, which will be displayed in the store, via an API call.
Automated notifications are sent to staff for proposals that have been pending review for a configurable duration.
Proposals exceeding 10 working days without verification are automatically moved to a 'rejected' status, and a specific rejection message is sent to the supplier.
Staff can use a barcode scanner or manual input to record the receipt of products against a purchase order, updating quantities and identifying discrepancies.
Staff can mark products as 'received' and specify their designated shelf or storage location within the inventory system via an API call.
Staff can log issues with received products (e.g., 'damaged', 'incorrect quantity', 'wrong item') and attach relevant details or images via an API endpoint.
Automated alerts are sent to staff when product inventory falls below a predefined minimum threshold.
Staff can create a new purchase order for specific products and quantities, selecting a supplier, via an API endpoint.
Staff can view system-generated reorder proposals and either approve them for placement or modify them before approval.
Staff can mark a purchase order as 'completed' and trigger the payment process to the supplier, sending a specific message to the supplier, once all items are confirmed received and accepted.
Staff can partially close a purchase order, indicating which items have been received and which are still pending, and schedule follow-ups, sending a specific message to the supplier.
Customers can view a list of available products, filter by categories, and search for specific items via the online store interface.
Customers can select a product and specify quantity to add it to their virtual shopping cart via an API call.
Customers can proceed to checkout, enter their shipping address, and confirm their order details via a dedicated API endpoint.

Customers can submit payment information (e.g., credit card details, Paypal, Satispay, La Reine Marlene purchasing card, immediate online bank transfer) through an integrated payment gateway, which securely processes the transaction.
Customers can view the current status and location of their shipped orders through a tracking interface, updated by shipping carriers.
Customers who consent to mobile phone number usage receive automated notifications on delivery time updates.
The Point-of-Sale (POS) system allows customers to select items, process payments, and receive receipts for in-store purchases.
Customers can create a new support ticket by providing their contact information, a subject, and a detailed description of their issue via a web form or API.
Customers can retrieve a list of their support tickets and view the latest updates and agent responses through a dedicated portal or API.
Customers can add comments or provide additional information to an open support ticket via the customer support portal or API.
Automated alerts are sent to agents when a new support ticket is assigned to them, including ticket details and customer information.
Agents can add internal notes or send direct replies to customers within a support ticket, updating its status as needed, within a 24-hour response window.
Agents can change the status of a ticket (e.g., 'open', 'in progress', 'resolved', 'closed') via an API call.
If a customer service agent does not respond to an assigned ticket within 24 hours, the system automatically reassigns the ticket to another available agent.
If a customer does not respond to an agent's reply on a support ticket within 5 working days, the system automatically closes the ticket.
Carriers can query the system to get a list of orders assigned to them for delivery, including customer addresses and product details.
Carriers can update the status of an order (e.g., 'shipped', 'in transit', 'out for delivery', 'delivered') via an API endpoint, which then updates customer tracking information.
Managers can retrieve detailed reports on all customer orders, including order volume, average order value, and order fulfillment times, via a reporting API.
Managers can generate reports on sales trends, revenue, and product performance over various time periods, using a data analytics dashboard.
Managers can view real-time inventory levels, stock turnover rates, and identify slow-moving or fast-moving products through an inventory management interface.
Managers can access reports on ticket resolution times, customer satisfaction scores, and common inquiry types to assess support team performance.
Administrators can set minimum stock thresholds, reorder quantities, and preferred suppliers for automated reordering via a configuration interface or API.
Administrators can define schedules for when the system should check stock levels and trigger automated reorders based on configured rules.
